## Shiny Documents

This Quarto document presents a workflow for the characterization and 
visualization of molecular networks. It includes the analysis of known
compounds detected in FT-MS data and their corresponding features in QTOF 
datasets, as well as the visualization of ion trap–based and QTOF-based neutral
loss analyses. The document further summarizes the results of CID spectral 
matching, describes the annotation and incorporation of characterized molecules 
into the database.

## Load required libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#' Load required libraries
library(devtools)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(here)
library(CompoundDb)
library(MsBackendMgf)
#rm(list = c("convert_compid_assoc"))
#` Uploading RDynLib: Load all functions of the RDynlib directory
load_all()
```


#FTMS flax negative
We start by loading the flax sql qtof and ftms data, the cspp file that contains 
the biochemical transformations, and the charge_file where we mention the charge 
of the known compound in our flax database:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
# maize FTneg
maize_ftneg <- here("data","zenodo", "maize_ftneg.sqlite")
con_mftneg <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), maize_ftneg)

# flax FTneg
flax_ftneg <- here("data","zenodo", "flax_ftneg.sqlite")
con_fft <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), flax_ftneg)

# flax QTOFneg
flax_qtofneg <- here("data","zenodo", "flax_qtofneg.sqlite")
con_fqt <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), flax_qtofneg)

cspp_ft <- here("data","cspp_flax.txt")
charge_file <- here("data", "ftms_all_compounds_RD.xlsx")
```

Extract the available experiments in the flax ftms database:
```{r}
get_expid(flax_ftneg)
```


Then we update the cspp table:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
cspp.tot_SQL(flax_ftneg, 266, mzerr = 0.01,
                         cspp = cspp_ft, peakwidth = 0.1, IntThres  = 0, mz_tol = 0.5,
                         dot_thresh = 0, spectrum_type = "pseudo_MS2",  
                         min_common = 0, charge_file = charge_file)
```

Update the gnps table:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
conv.GNPS_SQL(sql_path= flax_ftneg, expid = 266, peakwidth = 0.2, mzerr = 0.015,
              min = 5, adduct = 60.0211, thr1 = 2, thr2 = 0.1, thr3 = 0.3,
              spectrum_type = "individual", IntThres = 0)
```

Next we visualize the CSPP and GNPS network of 101238 compound from ftms neg:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#| #| dev: svg
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 15
Overall.net_SQL(sql_path = flax_ftneg, exp.id = 266, dbkey = 101280, min = 0,
                nr_of_seq = 3, thr1 = 0.1, thr2 = 0.2, thr3 = 0.3)
```

Based on the spectral similarity results performed in the **rdynlib_overview_workflow.qmd** 
workflow, the compound 101280 from ftms flax data had a high similarity with 
the 74905 refers to quercetin dihexoside compound from maize data.
Here we visualize the MSn spectra of both compounds:
```{r}
MSnplot_SQL(flax_ftneg, 101280, thr_int = 100)
```

```{r}
MSnplot_SQL(maize_ftneg, 74905, thr_int = 100)
```
The spectral plots shows a high similarity in MS2 level between 74905 and 101280,

Next, we print the plot the network of 101141 compound from the flax data, 
this compound has been detected in the cspp network of the 101280 compound:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#| #| dev: svg
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 15
Overall.net_SQL(sql_path = flax_ftneg, exp.id = 266, dbkey = 101141, min = 0,
                nr_of_seq = 3, thr1 = 0.1, thr2 = 0.2, thr3 = 0.3)
```

Now we show the ion trap based analysis of 101141 compound:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4
MSnplot_SQL(flax_ftneg, 101141, thr_int = 100)
```



#Qtof flax analysis

Import the qtof flax database and required files:
```{r}
# flax QTOFneg
flax_qtofneg <- here("data","zenodo", "flax_qtofneg.sqlite")
con_fqt <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), flax_qtofneg)

neutral_loss_candid <- here("data", "neutral_loss_candid.txt")
neutloss <- read.table(
  neutral_loss_candid,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

product_ion_candid <- here("data", "product_ion_candid_2.txt")
prdion <- read.table(
  product_ion_candid,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

```


The aligned compound of the 101141 compound from flax in qtof data corresponds
to 45889 compound from ftms data:
```{r}
alignment_file <- here("data", "flax_qtn_ftn_align.txt")

getAlignedCompids <- getAlignedCompids_SQL(
compound_id = 101141,
  database_name = "flax_ftneg.sqlite",
  alignment_file = alignment_file
)
getAlignedCompids
```
The 45890 is the qtof compound_id that was aligned with 100988 ftms compound_id. 

The msms_spectrum table linked to that compound_id to select the spectrum_id:
```{r}
list_spectrum <- get_spectrum_id(flax_qtofneg, 45889)
list_spectrum
```

We chose the 46001 spectrum_id to show the qtof based neutral loss analysis:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#| #| dev: svg
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8
res <- MSMSspecplot_SQL(flax_qtofneg, 45889, 
                 prdion = prdion, neutloss = neutloss, err = NULL, 
                 minum = NULL, nr_col = NULL,   nr_col2 = NULL)
```
print the neutral losses:
```{r}
output_text <- capture.output(
  res <- MSMSspecplot_SQL(
    flax_qtofneg, 45889,
    prdion = prdion,
    neutloss = neutloss,
    err = NULL,
    minum = NULL,
    nr_col = NULL,
    nr_col2 = NULL
  ),
  type = "output"
)

cat(output_text, sep = "\n")
```

Extract the experiment id:
```{r}
get_expid(flax_qtofneg)
```
Next, we show the molecular networks of the 45889 compound id:
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: "hide"
#| warning: false
#| #| dev: svg
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 15
Overall.net_SQL(sql_path = flax_qtofneg, exp.id = 52, dbkey = 45889, min = 0,
                nr_of_seq = 3, thr1 = 0.1, thr2 = 0.2, thr3 = 0.3)
```


Finaly, we enter the characterization of the compounds found to the database:
```{r}
EnterName_SQL(ft_path, CoMPID = 101143)
```
